summary:
Motiva's new 325 kbpd
Choreographing the intricate meshing of untried equipment during the commissioning of a new refinery sometimes experiences mis-steps. Motiva's troubled start-up of their 325 kbpd Port Arthur refinery expansion underscores this observation. Stung by equipment corrosion incurred during its initial operation, the new capacity now sits idle while the extent of damage is evaluated .

children.summary: : As of June 28th Although estimates of how long repair work will last are better left until Motiva completes its inspection assessments, guesses swirling in the media suggest an outage of at least six months, or a longer. As highlighted in the chart below, May's uptick in VLCC fixtures from the AG to the US Gulf withered to a trickle in June.

children.title: Vela fixed eight extra
children.summary: cargoes in 1q12 over stock build needs The large jump in AG-USG fixtures in May would have partially reflected Motiva preparing for the continuous crude flow of 325 kbpd into the new unit, which would require an additional five VLCC fixtures a month, assuming 100% Saudi and other AG crudes into the new unit. Indeed, Vela increased its AG-USG fixtures to 17 in May, or five to six cargoes above its 1q12 average, so this pattern seems consistent with the anticipated start-up of the new unit.

children.title: Jump in fixtures during
children.summary: May reflected higher crude run rate from anticipated start-up Of course, Motiva Port Arthur's operating difficulties and subsequent shutdown has left the refinery with 50 days of crude inventory for its original 275 kbpd plant. The extra crude would represent roughly $700 million of incremental working capital, so Motiva would be keen to reduce stocks by lowering import volumes.
